title: Waymo Taps Toyota to Produce Autonomous Robotaxis for Japan and UK

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock
Toyota Motor Corporation American Depositary Shares (Each representing ten Ordinary Shares)

summary:
Waymo will integrate its self-driving hardware directly into the assembly line of Toyota's Takaoka factory in Japan to manufacture a new fleet of electric bZ4X robotaxis. Testing and validation of the autonomous vehicles in Japan will begin in 2027, with deployment to the UK and other international markets to follow in subsequent years.

The agreement expands a collaboration established in April 2025 and provides Waymo with a second vehicle platform for its global expansion alongside the Jaguar I-PACE it currently tests in London and Japan. Beyond ride-hailing fleets, the two companies will also study the feasibility of incorporating autonomous driving technology into Toyota vehicles owned by individual consumers.

selectedTweets.text:
WAYMO TAPS TOYOTA TO BUILD ROBOTAXIS FOR JAPAN & THE UK

$GOOGL's Waymo is expanding its partnership with Toyota $TM, with plans to begin testing autonomous Toyota bZ4X electric vehicles in Japan in 2027, followed by deployment in the UK and potentially other markets.

Toyota will manufacture the vehicles at its Takaoka factory in Japan, where Waymo's self-driving hardware will also be installed.

The agreement builds on an initial partnership announced in April 2025. Waymo is already testing Jaguar I-PACE vehicles in Japan and London, but the Toyota deal gives it another vehicle platform for expanding internationally.

The companies also plan to explore bringing Waymo's autonomous technology to personally owned Toyota vehicles, potentially extending the partnership beyond robotaxis.

Initial testing will involve a small number of vehicles, with broader deployment details yet to be announced.

selectedTweets.text:
Waymo says Toyota will build its autonomous bZ4X at the Takaoka plant, with testing in Japan from 2027 and deployment to the UK and other markets planned for later years. The release covers who builds the cars and who runs the service. It does not say who will own them.

That is one of the questions I asked about China's Pony in today's piece. Its 2025 annual report said: "we currently serve passengers entirely with our self-owned robotaxi fleets." It expects future fleets to be largely owned by third-party fleet companies. Its capital spending in the first half of 2026, $44.6m, already exceeded the full-year 2025 total. Pony ties that spending to its seventh-generation fleet and to data centres and servers, and does not disclose how much went to cars.
